sources.note: QL5/QL1 Owner's Manual d1 (opened, text read): QL1 dimensions 468 mm x 272 mm x 562 mm (W x H x D); fader 100 mm motorized; rear panel p.16-17 (XLR-3-31 INPUT 1-16 female, XLR-3-32 OMNI OUT 1-8 male, Dante PRIMARY/SECONDARY etherCON, AC IN, power switch); Selected Channel [PAN] knob adjusts pan or L/R balance; an [ON] key on every strip; USER DEFINED keys. The manual's dimension drawing carries no connector coordinates, so every position below is read from the photos.

Rear, straight-on (assets-source/yamaha-ql1/photos/rear.jpg, 2000x1281). The rear panel is the io face: all 7 modelled ports and the power switch are on it. Isotropic scale 3.68 px/mm (the width 468 mm gives 3.59 and the height 272 mm gives 3.77, the photo is not perfectly orthographic, so expect +/- 5 mm); x from the body centre (px 995), y from the bottom of the feet (px 1160). in-mic-1/2 = INPUT 1 and 2 (top row of the right-hand block, input 1 is rightmost seen from behind, pitch 23.9 mm). out-main-l/r and out-mix-1 = OMNI OUT 1, 2, 3 (right-hand end of the male block on the left, pitch 25.5 mm): the catalog simplifies, which OMNI OUT carries which bus is a guess, the first three are used. dante-primary = PRIMARY etherCON. power-in = AC IN (IEC C14, V-lock). power = the rocker above the AC inlet (20.7 x 33.2 mm visible housing; protrusion d = 12 mm is an estimate).

Top, overhead (assets-source/yamaha-ql1/photos/top.jpg, 1689x2000): x scale 3.006 px/mm and y scale 3.062 px/mm, calibrated to the 468 mm width and 562 mm depth; top-face y runs from the rear (I/O) edge to the front. The photo has the rear at the TOP of the picture, but the face-local convention for a top face is seen from above with the I/O edge (the rear) at the BOTTOM, x right, y up: that is the photo rotated 180 degrees, so the photo x is mirrored, xMm = 468 - x_photo (photo x = (px - 140) / 3.006: fader/mute A 401.5 -> 66.5, PAN 337.7 -> 130.3, USER key 1 411.8 -> 56.2); y is already measured from the rear edge and is unchanged. Control mapping: fader-master = master fader A of the Master section (100 mm travel, position at mid-travel); mute-master = the [ON] key above fader A (it switches the channel on or off); balance-master = the Selected Channel [PAN] knob (manual: it adjusts pan or L/R balance); playback-usb = USER DEFINED key 1: the catalog id is logical-only, the console has no dedicated play button, user keys can be assigned to recorder functions, key 1 is the stand-in. Heights (h) of caps, knobs and keys are estimates, not visible in the overhead view.

Neutrik NC3FD-L-1 product page (opened): "Standardized D sized 24 mm panel cutout". The XLR receptacles in the photos are Neutrik D-series (NEUTRIK legible on the Rio3224-D2 front), so openingMm = 24 for the XLR ports. The NC3MD-L-1 (male) page says the same (https://www.neutrik.com/en/product/nc3md-l-1).
